questions.question: A text structure is the way information and ideas are what?
A passage explains a problem and then presents possible solutions. Which structure is used?
A text explains how two renewable energy sources are alike and different. Which structure fits?
A passage traces the steps for safely using a microscope. What structure is most likely?
An article explains that heavy rain caused a stream to overflow. Which structure is shown?
A paragraph lists the parts and features of a coral reef. Which structure is most likely?
Words such as “first,” “next,” and “finally” often signal what?
Words such as “because,” “therefore,” and “as a result” often signal what?
A passage uses “both,” “however,” and “unlike” to discuss two animals. Which structure is likely?
A heading reads “Challenges of Urban Gardening” followed by “Ways to Improve Soil.” What organization is suggested?
A biography describes events from childhood through adulthood. Which structure is primarily used?
A passage describes a drought, then lists its effects on farms and reservoirs. What structure is emphasized?
A chapter explains “ecosystem,” then gives its components and examples. Which structure is likely?
An article alternates between the benefits and drawbacks of two transportation options. What structure supports that purpose?
A writer describes a community’s recycling problem and evaluates collection programs. How is the information organized?
A student sees the words “after” and “later” and assumes a cause-and-effect structure. What should the student check?
choices: whether the text explains causation or only time order
whether the passage has a title
whether the writer uses first person

questions.question: A passage has a list of steps but also explains what happens if one is skipped. What can a reader conclude?
choices: sequence may be combined with cause and effect
it is necessarily compare and contrast

questions.question: An article first describes two regions separately, then compares their climates. Which statement is precise?
choices: the text combines description and comparison

questions.question: A student summarizes a process text by listing background facts but omitting the steps. What did the summary miss?
choices: the sequence central to the author’s explanation

questions.question: A passage states that a new schedule reduced wait times, then explains how. Which organization is most apparent?
